newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta shrugs off EMU worries, fears intervention.
newsitem.headline: Peseta shrugs off EMU worries, fears intervention.

text.p: The peseta strengthened against the mark in afternoon trade on Wednesday, shrugging off an earlier bout of EMU worries and as fears of Bank of Spain intervention around 85.00 per mark capped further weakness.
By 1645 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.66/68 per mark, after touching 85.00 earlier in the session and compared with levels seen late on Tuesday of 84.79/82.
Traders said the peseta had received support from denials that an EMU entry compromise deal involving Italy was in the works.
"The denials together with fear of intervention has lifted pressure on the peseta," said one trader.
The Financial Times published a report quoting unnamed senior monetary officials as saying Italy would be offered a deal that would delay its entry into EMU until 2000 or 2001.
Italy rejected the reports as false, unjustified and unfounded while Spain said it was sure it would be in the first wave for entry into a single currency.
Strength in the dollar was also buoying the peseta, traders said.
Against the dollar, the peseta was trading at 139.52/57, compared with late Tuesday levels of 139.14/19.
